thread.title_full: Police probe continues as area mourns three found dead at mobile home - NewsBreak

author: William F. West
title: Police probe continues as area mourns three found dead at mobile home - NewsBreak
text:
By William F. West ,
14 hours ago
Rocky Mount police are continuing an investigation to find out what caused the deaths of three people whose bodies were found earlier this week at the King’s Way mobile home community on the far west side of the city.
The news has led to an outpouring of reactions from the community on social media.
And Rocky Mount Mayor Sandy Roberson is among those expressing condolences online. Roberson said in a post on social media on Wednesday afternoon that his heart goes out to the family and loved ones affected by what he called a heartbreaking tragedy.
“Our entire community mourns this devastating loss and, together, we will keep everyone impacted in our prayers,” Roberson said.
“While no words can ease the pain of such a loss, moments like this remind us of the importance of continually evaluating how we can best serve and support our community,” Roberson said.
Additionally, Roberson said that he has asked Rocky Mount City Manager Elton Daniels to explore policy changes regarding utilities payments.
Roberson specifically is asking Daniels to review whether there are opportunities to provide greater flexibility to residents who are making a good-faith effort to pay their bills while also ensuring that any changes protect the integrity of the system and prevent abuse.
“As we learn more facts about this tragedy, our focus remains on supporting our neighbors, promoting public safety and working together to help prevent future tragedies,” Roberson said.
The police department as of Wednesday evening provided no new updates about the case and did not provide the names and ages of the deceased.
Television station WRAL on Tuesday reported that relatives identified two found dead inside the mobile home as a married couple, Tracey Swann and Kenny Swann. The third person, WRAL reported, was identified by relatives as Mahala Scurlock, 20, whom Tracey Swann had adopted.
Krista Crisp, who is a daughter of Tracey Swann, was quoted by the TV station as saying that her mother’s electricity had recently been turned off and that this could have played a role in the deaths.
Crisp also was quoted saying that the family’s utilities bill was more than $2,000 and that her mother was the only one working.
Crisp also was quoted saying that her mother tried to make partial payments, but that the city only would accept the full amount.
The city’s communications, marketing and public relations department on Wednesday evening declined to respond to emailed questions regarding the account at that residence, citing that state law specifies that customer utilities billing information is not a public record.
The city is in both the electric service and natural gas service business.
As of Wednesday evening, the only news release from the police department about the deaths came on Monday evening with the announcement that officers discovered the three bodies around 10:45 a.m. after conducting a welfare check at a residence off King Charles Court in King’s Way.
The mobile home community is off South Halifax Road between Sunset Avenue and Bethlehem Road.
Police on Monday said that the N.C. Office of the Chief Medical Examiner was notified.
The office investigates all deaths in the state that result from injury or violence, as well as natural deaths that are suspicious, unusual or unattended by a medical professional.
The deaths come amid the city announcing it was resuming utilities service disconnections for non-payment.
That announcement also followed N.C. Auditor Dave Boliek’s probe into the city’s utilities billing system.
Boliek, who released the findings of the audit on July 8, noted that his team found mistakes made by the utilities billing department that led to confusion regarding bills received by customers.
According to the findings of the audit, city officials on Dec. 15 found a significant gap between dates that the meters were read and the billing dates.
The city, after discovering the issue, sent utilities customers a bill for a number of days shorter than a typical billing cycle to eliminate the billing date discrepancy.
An outpouring of concern among residents flooded social media, and residents expressed confusion and frustration at several City Council hearings about receiving two bills in the same month or closer together than normal.
In January, Daniels told residents at a special-called council work session that the billing situation could have been handled better and that he looked at the experience as an opportunity for improvement.
Daniels in January also made clear that there were going to be no penalties for late payments and no disconnections of accounts with balances associated with the two bills that customers had received in the shorter timeframe.
summary: Roberson said in a post on social media on Wednesday afternoon that his heart goes out to the family and loved ones affected by what he called a heartbreaking tragedy. Roberson specifically is asking Daniels to review whether there are opportunities to provide greater flexibility to residents who are making a good-faith effort to pay their bills while also ensuring that any changes protect the integrity of the system and prevent abuse.
